required_seven_items.authors: Burkitt E, Barrett M, Davis A
required_seven_items.title: Children's colour choices for completing drawings of affectively characterised topics
required_seven_items.journal: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry
required_seven_items.sample_size: N=330, 3 conditions (colouring in a pre-drawn man/dog/tree outline)
required_seven_items.drawing_task: INSTRUCTED colouring-in-completion task with affectively characterised topic framing (e.g. 'a nice man' vs 'a nasty man'), not free drawing and not even free drawing-from-scratch (children coloured a pre-drawn outline)
required_seven_items.finding: Children systematically altered colour use across differently affectively-characterised topics; even young children used colour symbolically in a way that tracked the assigned emotional framing of the topic.
required_seven_items.limitation: Instructed, colouring-in-a-template task -- children were TOLD the topic's emotional framing, so this measures whether children CAN encode an externally-assigned emotion via colour on demand, not whether a child's unprompted, spontaneous colour choice reveals their own internal state.
required_seven_items.applicability_to_doar_free_drawings: NOT directly applicable to DOAR's colour_proportions/dominant_colour features on spontaneous free drawings -- the demonstrated effect required external emotional framing DOAR never provides. This is a DIFFERENT Burkitt-related study from the one already catalogued in LITERATURE_CANDIDATE_REGISTER.csv as LIT_COLOUR_EMOTION_001 (DOI 10.1080/01443410.2013.785059, Educational Psychology 2014) -- do not conflate the two; both are real, distinct papers.
required_seven_items.used_for: Paired with REF_CRAWFORD_COLOUR_CAUTION_2012 below (see also LIT_COLOUR_EMOTION_001) to show the colour/emotion literature is directly contested, not simply supportive -- no DOAR colour-based emotion rule is justified by either side alone.
required_seven_items.verification_status: VERIFIED_THIS_SESSION -- exact citation (JCPP 44(3):445-455, 2003), authors, and DOI cross-confirmed via independent web search (ACAMH/Wiley + Semantic Scholar).

required_seven_items.authors: Crawford E, Gross J, Patterson T, Hayne H
required_seven_items.title: Does Children's Colour Use Reflect the Emotional Content of Their Drawings?
required_seven_items.sample_size: Not independently re-derived from full text this session (search-summary level only)
required_seven_items.drawing_task: INSTRUCTED colouring-in task (colouring outlines characterised as 'nice' vs 'nasty')
required_seven_items.finding: Children used more of their PREFERRED colours on the 'nice' outline and more NON-preferred colours on the 'nasty' outline, but for both outlines used a MIX of preferred and non-preferred colours -- i.e. colour use did not cleanly or reliably track emotional valence on its own. Explicit authors' caution: colour use alone should not be treated as a reliable emotional indicator.
required_seven_items.limitation: Same instructed-task caveat as the Burkitt et al. 2003 study above; this is the DIRECT CAUTIONARY counterpoint the task asked to compare against it, not a free-drawing study either.
required_seven_items.applicability_to_doar_free_drawings: NOT directly applicable as a positive method, but highly applicable as a CAUTION: even in a paradigm MORE favourable to detecting a colour/emotion link (instructed, externally-framed) than DOAR's free-drawing context, colour use only partially and inconsistently tracked emotion. DOAR's existing colour_proportions/dominant_colour features must never be presented as an emotion indicator without exactly this caveat.
required_seven_items.used_for: Direct comparison against REF_BURKITT_BARRETT_DAVIS_2003 (and the pre-existing LIT_COLOUR_EMOTION_001 entry) -- the colour/emotion literature is genuinely mixed/contested, not simply supportive with one skeptical footnote. No DOAR colour-based emotion rule exists today; this pair of references is why none should be added without much stronger, free-drawing-specific evidence.
required_seven_items.verification_status: VERIFIED_THIS_SESSION -- exact citation (Infant and Child Development 21:198-215, 2012), authors, and DOI cross-confirmed via independent web search (Semantic Scholar + ResearchGate + Springer citation).

required_seven_items.authors: Philippsen A, Tsuji S, Nagai Y
required_seven_items.title: Quantifying developmental and individual differences in spontaneous drawing completion among children
required_seven_items.sample_size: N=104 children (62M/42F), 621 drawings; 107 drawings from 5 adults
required_seven_items.drawing_task: Drawing-COMPLETION paradigm: children complete a partially-drawn stimulus (outline-only / inner-features-shown / scrambled-inner-features) across 4 object categories (face, house, car, human figure). NOT pure free drawing (a stimulus is always present) and NOT verbally instructed either -- a distinct third category from both of DOAR's PDF sources' framing.
required_seven_items.finding: Representational drawing content increases and scribbling decreases with age (p<.001), measured via CNN-extracted hierarchical visual features. No correlation found between drawing behaviour and autistic-trait (AQ) scores in this sample.
required_seven_items.limitation: Purely developmental/maturational, explicitly not proposed by the authors as an emotional or diagnostic indicator. Measurement method (CNN-extracted features) differs from DOAR's classical handcrafted features (stroke/fragmentation/connected-component) -- whether DOAR's existing features capture the same construct is an untested, open hypothesis, not an established fact.
required_seven_items.applicability_to_doar_free_drawings: PARTIALLY APPLICABLE at most: the underlying developmental phenomenon is robust in the source population/protocol, but transfer to DOAR's own features and to genuinely unrestricted free drawing (no stimulus at all) is unvalidated and would need a DOAR-specific pilot.
required_seven_items.used_for: Developmental/confounding context for interpreting drawing maturity -- explicitly NOT a psychiatric or diagnostic reference. Already catalogued as LIT_DEVELOPMENTAL_STAGE_OBJECTIVE_006.
required_seven_items.verification_status: VERIFIED (carried forward) -- full text was read directly via PMC in the prior session per LITERATURE_CANDIDATE_REGISTER.csv; journal (Frontiers in Psychology) and PMID cross-confirmed independently this session.

scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.authors: Multiple (see note) -- Koppitz's own original text not directly retrieved
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.title: Koppitz Emotional Indicators reliability/validity literature (aggregated from multiple secondary validation studies found this session)
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.journal: Multiple (e.g. Journal of Personality Assessment; secondary validation studies)
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.population: Children, multiple studies, general clinical and community samples
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.sample_size: Aggregated across multiple independent validation studies, not a single N
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.finding: A validated, standardized 30-item composite scoring system exists (Koppitz's Emotional Indicators). Inter-scorer reliability reported acceptable (phi 0.75-0.81 across 3 judges in one validation study). Test-retest reliability was POOR for 28 of the 30 individual indicators AND the total score (phi <0.43). The indicator system fails to discriminate MILDLY disturbed children's drawings from typical children matched for age; it only shows a group-level difference for SEVERELY disturbed children vs. typical controls. One study found school psychologists could not distinguish counseling-referred pupils' drawings from non-referred pupils' drawings by clinical inspection alone.
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.limitation: This IS a real, standardized, widely-studied multi-indicator scoring system (directly relevant to this audit's Section 5 request) -- but its own validation literature finds POOR test-retest reliability and NO discriminative validity except at the severe end of disturbance. A structurally similar DOAR feature (counting multiple weak indicators together) would inherit the same reliability concern unless independently re-validated.
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.applicability_to_doar_free_drawings: NOT directly usable -- instructed DAP protocol, requires a full body-part-presence/distortion/size-anomaly detector far beyond DOAR's current roadmap, and the system's OWN validation shows weak reliability even in its native context. The GENERAL PRINCIPLE (structured multi-indicator counting, reported transparently rather than as a single score) is the only transferable element -- see EVIDENCE_AGGREGATION_POLICY.md.
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.used_for: RULE_EVIDENCE_AUDIT.md Section 5 (published scoring systems); EVIDENCE_AGGREGATION_POLICY.md (why DOAR borrows the STRUCTURE of multi-indicator counting, never Koppitz's specific items or any numeric weight).
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.verification_status: VERIFIED_THIS_SESSION -- multiple independent secondary sources (SAGE Journals, digitalcommons.cwu.edu, PubMed 5331280) cross-confirm the reliability/validity figures reported here; Koppitz's own 1968 primary text was not directly retrieved.

scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.authors: Naglieri JA, McNeish TJ, Bardos AN
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.title: Draw-A-Person: Screening Procedure for Emotional Disturbance (DAP:SPED)
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.journal: Standardized assessment manual; validity studies published separately (e.g. McNeish & Naglieri 1993, Matto/Naglieri/Clausen 2005)
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.population: Children/adolescents, multiple validation samples (e.g. one study: N=68 latency-age children 6-12 in counseling/treatment settings)
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.sample_size: Multiple independent validation studies, not a single N
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.finding: A standardized, quantitative multi-item scoring system for emotional-disturbance screening from three DAP figures. Some studies found the total DAP:SPED score a significant, moderate-strength predictor of internalizing behavioral disturbance; other studies report correlations with emotional-difficulty measures are 'at best small, resulting in inadequate diagnostic accuracy' as a screening tool.
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.limitation: Mixed validity evidence even within its own native, instructed, standardized context -- not a settled, universally-endorsed scoring system.
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.applicability_to_doar_free_drawings: NOT directly usable -- instructed, standardized three-figure protocol; requires a full figure-quality/proportion detector DOAR does not have. Same GENERAL PRINCIPLE point as Koppitz above: the value is in the existence proof that structured, multi-item, transparently-reported drawing scoring systems are a real, published methodology -- not in any borrowable item, cutoff, or weight.
scoring_system_references_new_this_sessi.verification_status: VERIFIED_THIS_SESSION -- authors, standardized-system name, and mixed-validity finding cross-confirmed via independent web search (PubMed 12056084, SAGE Journals, ResearchGate).
